sections.1.heading: When a Zoho Invoice alternative makes sense
sections.1.body:
Before you look for a **Zoho Invoice alternative**, it's worth being clear about what you'd be leaving. Zoho invoicing software is hard to beat on price: Zoho Invoice is free. According to [its pricing page](https://www.zoho.com/us/invoice/pricing/), checked on 28 November 2026, it includes time tracking and projects, online payments, a customer portal, recurring invoices, and apps for iOS, Android, Windows and Mac. For many small businesses, that's everything they need.

The free plan has limits, set out in the page's FAQ: up to two users, a maximum of three projects, and up to 500 invoices a year. Those limits are often the moment a team starts comparing tools. A third person joins, a fourth project starts, and the free tool no longer fits the team.

Paidlyo is built for exactly that stage: agencies, studios and consultancies with a handful to a few dozen people who bill clients by the hour. It isn't free. It costs $9 per person a month, with unlimited people, clients, projects and invoices. This page explains when that's worth paying for, and when it isn't.
sections.2.heading: Who should stay on Zoho Invoice
sections.2.body:
We'd rather you stay on a free tool that suits you than pay for one that doesn't. Zoho Invoice is likely the better choice if:

- **You work alone or with one other person** and don't expect that to change soon
- **You have three or fewer active projects** at a time
- **Clients pay by card online,** which Zoho Invoice supports and Paidlyo doesn't
- **You bill the same amount every month,** where recurring invoices save time
- **You want a client portal or mobile apps,** which Paidlyo doesn't have

Paidlyo also lacks some things Zoho Invoice lists, such as card payments and recurring invoices. Every Paidlyo invoice is built from tracked hours, and clients pay you directly, by bank transfer or however you agree, before you record the payment.

If several of the points above describe your business, keep using Zoho Invoice. If you've hit the user or project limits and your billing is mostly hours, read on.
sections.2.callout: Count your people and active projects before you compare tools. If you're within two users and three projects, a free plan may cover you completely.
sections.3.heading: Where growing teams outgrow the free plan
sections.3.body:
Here is an illustrative studio at three stages of growth, compared with the free plan's limits:

| Stage | People | Active projects | Within Zoho Invoice's free limits? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Founder and one designer | 2 | 3 | Yes |
| First developer joins | 3 | 5 | No: users and projects |
| Small studio | 6 | 12 | No: users and projects |

At the second stage, the studio has a choice: move to another Zoho product, or move to a tool built for its kind of work. Zoho offers paid products such as Zoho Books and Zoho Projects, so check their current pricing if you want to stay in the Zoho family.

If you choose Paidlyo, the cost grows with the team in a straight line: $27 a month for three people, $54 for six, $108 for twelve, with nothing else to upgrade. Every feature is included from the first person.

Price isn't the only thing to weigh. Moving tools takes an afternoon of setup and a few weeks for new habits to settle. If you expect to stay at two or three people for the next year, that effort may not be worth it. If you're hiring, it's easier to switch before the team doubles than after.
sections.4.heading: How Paidlyo handles time-based billing for teams
sections.4.body:
Paidlyo is narrower than Zoho Invoice, and deliberately so. It focuses on one flow: tracking hours across a team and turning them into invoices.

1. **Everyone tracks time** with a browser timer or a weekly timesheet, against a client, project and task, marked billable or not.
2. **Rates are set per project or per task,** so strategy and production can have different prices.
3. **Projects can have budgets,** so you can compare hours used with what was agreed.
4. **Invoices are built from unbilled hours** in one click, grouped by project, task or person, with your logo, discount, tax and the client's currency.
5. **Clients open invoices through a private link** without an account, and can save a PDF.
6. **You record payments,** in full or in part, and see outstanding invoices by age.

Reports show hours by client, project and task, plus unbilled time, and everything exports to CSV for your accountant or a spreadsheet. There's more on how the tracking side works in [Paidlyo time tracking](/time-tracking), and on the billing side in [how invoices are built from tracked time](/invoicing).
sections.5.heading: Switching from Zoho Invoice to Paidlyo
sections.5.body:
There's no direct import from Zoho Invoice; Paidlyo's importer reads Harvest CSV files. For a small team, starting fresh is usually quick:

1. **Export your history from Zoho Invoice,** such as invoices and time records, and keep it as an archive.
2. **Add your active clients and projects** in Paidlyo, with tasks, hourly rates and each client's currency.
3. **Invite your team** with owner, admin or member roles.
4. **Start tracking on the first day of a month,** so that month's invoices all come from one tool.
5. **Finish open invoices in Zoho Invoice,** and record payments for them there.

Use the 14-day trial to run a full billing cycle before you decide. A card is needed to start the trial, and nothing is charged until it ends.

If the main reason you're moving is to bill more of your team's time, see how [billable hours tracking](/features/billable-hours) works in Paidlyo.

sections.1.heading: When a Wave alternative makes sense
sections.1.body:
If you're weighing up a **Wave alternative**, start with what Wave already gives you. Wave invoicing software is popular with small businesses because its Starter plan is free. According to [Wave's pricing page](https://www.waveapps.com/pricing), checked on 28 November 2026, Starter includes unlimited estimates, invoices and bills, and unlimited bookkeeping records. The Pro plan costs $19 a month, or $190 a year, and adds things like online payments sent through Wave, automatic late payment reminders, your own branding and bank transaction imports.

People look elsewhere for different reasons. For agencies, studios and consultancies, a common one is time. Wave's pricing page doesn't list time tracking, and for a team that bills by the hour, the hours are where every invoice starts. Without them in the same tool, someone copies numbers from a timesheet into each invoice every month.

Paidlyo is built around that problem. Your team tracks time against clients, projects and tasks, and invoices are built from the unbilled hours. It doesn't do bookkeeping, payroll or card payments, so it isn't a full replacement for Wave. For many service teams, the right setup is to keep the accounting where it is and move the hourly billing.
sections.2.heading: Who should stay on Wave
sections.2.body:
Wave covers a lot for very little money. It's likely the better fit if:

- **You need bookkeeping and invoicing in one place.** Paidlyo has no accounting features.
- **You sell products or fixed-price services,** where invoices don't start from hours.
- **Clients pay by card online.** Wave processes card payments, with fees listed on its pricing page. Paidlyo doesn't take card payments.
- **You want payroll in the same tool.** Wave offers it as a paid add-on.
- **You work alone or with one or two people** and rarely bill by the hour.

In those cases, adding Paidlyo would mean paying for a second tool to solve a problem you don't really have. Stay with Wave.

Paidlyo makes more sense once several people track time for clients, rates differ by project or task, and building invoices from timesheets is taking real hours each month.
sections.3.heading: Using Paidlyo with Wave, or instead of it
sections.3.body:
Because Paidlyo doesn't do accounting, a team that moves hourly billing to Paidlyo will still need bookkeeping somewhere. There are three possible setups:

| Setup | How it works | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Paidlyo for time and invoices, Wave for books | Invoice clients from Paidlyo, then record invoices and payments in Wave | Some double entry each month, as there's no integration |
| Paidlyo for time only, Wave for invoices | Track hours in Paidlyo, export them to CSV, build invoices in Wave | You lose invoices built straight from tracked hours |
| Paidlyo instead of Wave | Use Paidlyo for time and invoices, and a different tool or accountant for books | You need another bookkeeping solution |

The first setup keeps each tool doing what it's best at. The cost is a monthly step where someone enters invoice totals and payments into the books, using Paidlyo's CSV exports of outstanding invoices as a check.

Talk to whoever does your books before you change anything. They'll tell you which setup is least work for them.
sections.3.callout: Paidlyo has no integration with Wave, QuickBooks or Xero. Plan who records invoices in your books before you switch, not after.
sections.4.heading: What it costs for a team
sections.4.body:
Wave's Pro plan is a flat monthly price on its pricing page, while Paidlyo charges per person. For a small team, that makes Wave cheaper on paper:

| Team size | Wave Starter | Wave Pro, monthly | Paidlyo, monthly |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 people | $0 | $19 | $18 |
| 5 people | $0 | $19 | $45 |
| 10 people | $0 | $19 | $90 |

That's not the whole comparison, though. If your team bills hours, you'd also need a time tracker alongside Wave, and someone to move hours into invoices every month. Count both the second tool's price and that person's time.

For a 5-person team billing 400 hours a month, saving even two hours of invoicing work at $60 an hour is worth more than the price difference. If your team doesn't bill hours, the numbers point the other way, and Wave is the better deal.

The other hidden cost is lost hours. When time is tracked in one place and invoiced in another, small amounts of billable work slip through: a call nobody copied over, a task logged to the wrong client. Seeing every unbilled hour in one report before you invoice can be where the real return comes from, more than any difference in subscription price. There's more on that in [billable hours tracking](/features/billable-hours).
sections.5.heading: Getting started if Paidlyo fits

2. **Create projects and tasks** with hourly rates, and budgets where you've agreed them.
3. **Invite your team** with owner, admin or member roles.
4. **Track time for a full month,** with the timer for focused work and the weekly timesheet for the rest.
5. **Create your first invoices** from unbilled hours, share them as links, and record them in your books.

The 14-day trial is enough to test the tracking habit and see your first unbilled time report. A card is needed to start, and nothing is charged until the trial ends.

For some businesses, that level of visibility is exactly the point.

Teams often move away for one of two reasons. Some find that monitoring hurts trust: good people feel watched, and the activity numbers start to matter more than the work. Others realise they never needed monitoring in the first place. What they need is to know which client and project each hour belongs to, so they can bill it.

Paidlyo is built for that second need. People log their own time with a browser timer or a weekly timesheet, against a client, project and task, marked billable or not. sections.1.heading: When a Paymo alternative makes sense
sections.1.body:
If you're looking for a **Paymo alternative**, it helps to start with what Paymo covers. Paymo time tracking software is part of a wider work management tool. According to [Paymo's pricing page](https://www.paymoapp.com/pricing/), checked on 28 November 2026, its plans include task management, time tracking and invoicing, with Kanban boards, Gantt charts, resource scheduling, recurring invoices and expenses on its higher tiers. It also has mobile and desktop apps.

That's a lot of tool, and for some teams it's exactly right: one place to plan the work, track it and bill it. Teams often start comparing tools when they don't use half of it. Perhaps they already plan projects in a separate tool the whole company uses, and Paymo's task management sits empty while they pay for it.

Paidlyo is built for that situation. It doesn't try to manage tasks or schedules. It does time tracking and billing: a browser timer and weekly timesheet by client, project and task, rates and budgets, invoices from unbilled hours, payment recording and reports. All of it costs $9 per person a month, with every feature on one plan.

If you want planning, time and billing in one tool, Paymo may suit you better. If you want a focused tracker alongside the planning tool you already have, read on.
sections.2.heading: One all-in-one tool, or two focused tools?
sections.2.body:
This is the real decision, and it depends on where your team already works:

| Your current setup | Likely better choice |
|---|---|
| You plan work nowhere yet, or in spreadsheets | An all-in-one tool like Paymo |
| You plan in a separate project tool everyone uses | A focused tracker like Paidlyo |
| You need Gantt charts and staff scheduling | Paymo Pro or another planning tool |
| You mainly need hours, rates, budgets and invoices | Paidlyo |

Running two tools has a cost: people need to know where to log time, and project names should match in both. Keep the same project names in both tools, and the overlap stays small. Running one large tool has a cost too: more settings, more training, and paying for features some people never open.

Neither is wrong. Pick the setup that matches how your team already plans work, rather than changing everyone's habits for a billing tool.

A quick test helps: ask three people on the team where they look first each morning to see what they're working on. If they all name the same planning tool, and it isn't Paymo, a focused tracker next to it is likely the simpler setup.
sections.3.heading: What you give up by leaving Paymo
sections.3.body:
Before you switch, check what Paidlyo doesn't have:

- **Task management.** No task lists, Kanban boards, Gantt charts or dependencies. Paidlyo tasks are categories for time and rates, not to-do items.
- **Resource scheduling.** No staff scheduling or workload planning.
- **Recurring invoices and expenses.** Every Paidlyo invoice is built from tracked hours, and there's no expense tracking.
- **Apps and integrations.** No mobile or desktop apps, no integrations and no public API. Paidlyo runs in a web browser and exports CSV.
- **A free plan.** Paymo has one for one user, one client and two projects. Paidlyo has a 14-day trial instead, with a card needed to start.

What you keep is the billing core: time by client, project and task, rates per project or task, project budgets, invoices built from unbilled hours with your logo, tax and the client's currency, partial payments and outstanding invoices by age.

sections.4.heading: What a team pays
sections.4.body:
Paymo's pricing page shows introductory prices for the first three months, then regular monthly prices of $15.90 per user for Plus and $23.90 per user for Pro. It also mentions annual discounts of up to 40%, without listing annual prices. Using the regular monthly prices:

| Team size | Paymo Plus, a year | Paymo Pro, a year | Paidlyo, monthly billing, a year |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 people | $954 | $1,434 | $540 |
| 10 people | $1,908 | $2,868 | $1,080 |
| 20 people | $3,816 | $5,736 | $2,160 |

On yearly billing, Paidlyo costs $90 per person, so a 10-person team pays $900. Paymo's annual discount would narrow the gap, so check its current annual prices before you compare.

Remember to add the cost of your planning tool if you'd use Paidlyo alongside one. If that tool is already paid for, paying for Paymo's planning features as well means paying twice for the same job.
sections.5.heading: Switching from Paymo to Paidlyo
sections.5.body:
There's no direct import from Paymo; Paidlyo's importer reads Harvest CSV files. For a small team, setting up fresh is straightforward:

1. **Export your time entries and invoices from Paymo** and keep them as your history.
2. **Add your active clients and projects** in Paidlyo, using the same project names as your planning tool.
3. **Add tasks, hourly rates and budgets.** Keep tasks broad, such as design, development and meetings.
4. **Invite the team** with owner, admin or member roles, and agree a start date.
5. **Start on the first day of a month,** and finish the current month's invoices in Paymo.

There's more on setting up projects, rates and budgets in [project time tracking](/features/project-time-tracking), and on billing in [how Paidlyo invoicing works](/invoicing). Agencies can also read [time tracking for agencies](/time-tracking/for/agencies) for rate cards and scope creep. Try it with the 14-day trial before you cancel anything.
